subject: Mutual Action Plan — unit-econ sanity checks & MAP close runway
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@cardiotech.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cardiotech.com
Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: MAP & cost modelling kick-off (tokens/$, caching, batching)

Hi Jasmine / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CardioTech is excited about the latency and reliability profile you showed. Our procurement lead asked that we get a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that specifically calls out the unit economics assumptions (tokens per request, tokens/$ table, expected cache hit assumptions, batching opportunities) so we can align internally on budget and procurement milestones.

High-level asks from our side:
- A table showing tokens per API call for the three flows we discussed (triage prompt, context-retrieval + prompt, streaming summary) with low/med/high traffic scenarios.
- Caching assumptions: what prefix/KV caching would save us (estimates for 50/70/90% cache-hit).
- Batching: expected throughput gains and latency tradeoffs for 4, 8, 16 request batches.
- Timeline: we need a POC and procurement signoff before Oct 15 to meet our Q4 launch.

Can you share a MAP draft and an evaluation plan that includes concrete token-econ checks we can review with engineering and procurement? Also cc'ing procurement for visibility.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Integrations
CardioTech

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 10:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & cost modelling kick-off (tokens/$, caching, batching)

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a first-pass MAP that maps deliverables to owners and dates. High-level response inline below.

Quick answers:
- Tokens per call: we will run passthrough estimates during the eval using representative prompts you provided. For an initial planning table we will assume: triage=350 tokens, retrieval+prompt=1,200 tokens, streaming summary=450 tokens (these are conservative med-case estimates).
- Caching: prefix/KV cache reduces tokens by reusing initial encodings for repeat sessions — typical savings 20–60% depending on user repetition. We'll model 50/70/90% hit-rate scenarios in the MAP.
- Batching: for latency-sensitive flows we recommend small batches (4–8) to keep p50 under 250ms; for high-throughput non-interactive flows we can batch to 16–32 for 2–3x cost savings.

Deliverables and timeline (draft):
- Today (03 Sep): MAP draft attached (CT-4521-MAP-draft.xlsx).
- Week of 06 Sep: Redwood runs baseline token-econ sims (Ben) and shares tokens/$ table for three traffic profiles.
- 09–17 Sep: Joint eval run (CardioTech + Redwood) to validate cache hit assumptions and latency with representative traces.
- 20 Sep: Procurement pricing alignment; draft commercial terms for POC.
- By Oct 12–15: Target procurement signoff.

Ben and Grace — can you pick up the unit-econ sims and a short rack of experiments (batch sizes [4,8,16], cache hit scenarios for 50/70/90%)? I can host a shared Drive folder and sync on Friday.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & cost modelling kick-off (tokens/$, caching, batching)

Got it — I'll run the sims. Quick checklist for CardioTech data we need to make the tokens/$ outputs meaningful:
1) QPS expected per flow (triage / retrieval / streaming) for low/med/high.
2) Typical prompt & response lengths (sample payloads if available).
3) Distribution of repeated prompts (to model cache hit). If you have client IDs or session IDs we can bucket reuse.
4) Concurrency & latency SLOs (p50,p95).
5) Any required model variants (e.g., one cheaper distil variant for fallback).

Assumptions I'll validate and expose in the spreadsheet:
- Model cost per 1M tokens for primary model (baseline) and fallback model.
- Effective tokens charged after prefix/KV cache applied.
- Batching multipliers (2x/2.5x cost reduction for 8/16 batch sizes) with latency impacts (rough p50 estimates).

I'll create a short 'unit_econ_assumptions.md' and a tokens-per-call table and drop both in the Drive. Planning to share by EOD Monday (07 Sep).

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 06 Sep 2026 13:05:00 -0700

Thanks Jasmine — quick clarifications from procurement/engineering as we prepare the joint eval: 

1) Security: we need SOC2 evidence and a KMS integration note for the POC. Can you point us to the audit docs?
2) Budget sensitivity: procurement wants two pricing envelopes — one with a conservative cost floor (no caching, low batching) and one with an optimistic savings scenario (70% cache-hit + batch=16).
3) Fallback model request: if Redwood can auto-fallback to a lower-cost model on overload, please specify which model and the expected tokens/$ delta.

We'll upload a small trace to the shared Drive by Tue (07 Sep) with anonymized session IDs so your sims can pick up realistic reuse patterns.

Also attaching our internal budget doc for context.

On the timeline: Oct 15 is firm for the program go/no-go. If the MAP and evaluation show >25% cost reduction opportunity with acceptable latency tradeoffs, procurement will prioritize the POC contract.

— Alex

Key decisions captured in MAP v2:

- If eval shows >20% improvement under 70% hit with p95 <= 1s for interactive flows, CardioTech will move to procurement review the week of Sep 20.
